title: Myelin basic protein expression in thymoma after methylprednisolone administration for multiple sclerosis
case_prompt:
A 39-year-old woman presented with dysarthria and dysgraphia of the right hand. She had no significant medical history. On examination, vital signs were stable, and neurologic assessment was notable only for mild slurring of speech and difficulty writing with the right hand.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the head showed a high-intensity lesion with rim enhancement in the left corona radiata on diffusion-weighted and T2-weighted images, and a separate high-intensity lesion in the right cerebral cortex without enhancement. Cerebrospinal fluid testing revealed elevated myelin basic protein, negative anti-aquaporin-4 antibodies, and positive oligoclonal IgG bands. One criterion for multiple sclerosis was fulfilled: dissemination in time and space. Intravenous methylprednisolone (500 mg daily for 3 days, then two courses of 1000 mg for 3 days) was administered, and her symptoms improved; follow-up MRI showed persistent lesions but resolution of the ring enhancement.

Routine chest computed tomography performed before steroid administration demonstrated a 30 mm homogeneous, hypodense mass with smooth contours and heterogeneous enhancement in the anterosuperior mediastinum. Serum soluble interleukin-2 receptor, carcinoembryonic antigen, and anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody levels were within normal limits. A thymoma was suspected, and video-assisted thoracoscopic thymectomy was planned.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Multiple sclerosis was suspected due to typical demyelinating lesions and CSF findings — “one criteria for MS was fulfilled; dissemination in time and space.”  
2. Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder was considered but deemed unlikely because of negative aquaporin-4 antibodies — “cerebrospinal fluid testing was … negative for anti-aquaporin-4 antibodies.”  
3. Anti-gamma aminobutyric acid A receptor antibody-positive encephalitis was included in the differential but was less consistent with her rapid steroid response and stable follow-up — “after differential diagnosis including … anti-gamma aminobutyric acid A receptor antibody-positive encephalitis … based on good clinical courses.”  
4. Other autoimmune encephalitides were considered but excluded by the absence of typical autoantibodies and continued clinical stability without further immunotherapy — “differential diagnosis including … autoimmune encephalitis … based on good clinical courses.”
